correctness.rationale: A coordinate of weight >=p proves the baseline at once. In the remaining light-stake case, p>1/5 and all triples are winning. Every pair is winning for p<=1/4. For p>1/4 sorted weights yield at least six winning pairs, giving F(p)=p(p-1)(3p²-5p+1)>F(1/4)=3/256. The explicit four-near-quarter one-vanishing-weight family proves sharp nonattainment, while a dominant weight attains the baseline. The exact rational checker reproduced the algebra and 103746 finite cases but is not relied upon as proof of continuum quantifiers.

value.rationale: A recent paper explicitly asks for the complete p<=1/3 inequality for arbitrary numbers of weights. Proving it for every p with at most five nonzero stakes is a natural meaningful cutoff, and the quantitatively sharp unattained 3/256 light-stake gap explains why any counterexample must involve at least six stakes. This combines a structural six-pair certificate with a sharp boundary family, rather than a routine isolated substitution.
